text.p: These are the leading stories of Albania's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters does not vouch for the accuracy of these stories.
KOHA JONE

- A government official said Interior Minister Belul Celo, who has denied he has quit his job, confirmed he would be back at his office on Thursday evening. He declined to say whether Celo was abroad.
- Socialist Party leader Fatos Nano told cheering crowds celebrating the Socialist victory in general elections they would learn from the mistakes of their predecessors.
- The Socialist Party would take over power from the Democratic Party but it faced a mountain of problems ahead, an editorial in the paper said.
- Albanian President Sali Berisha said he would resign after carrying out his constitutional duties.

- Supporters of exiled king Leka, who wants to reinstate the monarchy, held an unauthorised rally in central Skanderbeg Square that ended without incident despite the presence of heavy weapons in the square.
- Finance Ministry specialists said the three country's state banks will be sold for one dollar. The debts of these banks are bigger than their real sale price.
- The Albanian lek is gaining ground on the dollar after the general elections won by the Socialist Party. The dollar was firmed to 173 leks to the dollar on Wednesday from 180 on Sunday.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- A fire developed near oil tankers in the southern town of Vlore and firefighters and inhabitants fought hard to put out the flames.

- Supporters of the monarchy blocked a main road to the north, protesting that the monarchy had won a referendum on the to return the king to the throne but allege that the Socialists had manipulated the results.
- Italian authorities seized five tonnes of marihuana smuggled out of Albania since the beginning of the year.

- Several people have been treated for intestine typhus in Tirana's hospital. Doctors said they are not worried by the cases which are occuring after a typhus-free period but appealed for urgent measures in treating water.
ALBANIA
- The paper's headline reads: (Socialist leader Fatos) Nano: The Tanks towards the North. Yesterday afternoon the army was ordered to crack down on a monarchist revolt.

- A leader of the rightist National Front Party said they would back the Democratic Party in the second round of parliamentary elections. The Democrats were heavily beaten in the first by their leftist rivals, the Socialists.
- Armed gangs are exercising violence and terror against members of the Democratic Party.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- Albanian President Sali Berisha said elections were far from being normal.
- Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has accepted the nomination of Ali Kazazi as Interior Minister after incumbent Belul Celo was away from his office throughout Wednesday.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Nano told cheering supporters celebrating their victory in parliamentary elections they would keep their promises.
